title: Introducing Ruby's NEW Hand-Me-Down 1,500 Horsepower Texas Speed 7.0L

notes.fact: Filmed during COVID distancing; work done at Cleetus's home shop
Side segment: a junk 'parts runner' car bought to haul parts (no price stated)

base_vehicle.note: Corvette per series title/context; not stated in transcript

engine.rotating_assembly: Texas Speed off-the-shelf pistons and rods, stock crank, aftermarket cam

tune.note: described as too aggressive; plan was to pull timing and add boost (friend suggested ~35 psi)

power_adder.boost_psi_max: ~30 (never above 30 in Ruby before this test)

passes.note: best on this setup, stated as 'an 8-3' (8.3x)
test pass aborted: poor 60 ft, head gasket pushing coolant, temp rising

failures.cause: blown at high boost/timing; sticky paper-like coating blown off the gasket, head not torched; block deck may be warped -> deck resurface

engine.block: aluminum block, sleeved by Texas Speed (caption mentions 'Dart'; exact block wording garbled, low confidence)
engine.head_studs: upgraded to 1/2-inch head studs (was smaller when in Leroy)
engine.history: Leroy's original engine; claimed ~1,500 hp in Leroy; ran Leroy's first 7-second pass after blowing a head gasket, with coolant drained from the block

swap_notes.fact: Reused Ruby's oil pan, pickup tube, windage tray, balancer, relocated coil packs; new front cover; Texas Speed valve covers later
Pickup-tube O-ring stressed as critical for LS oil pressure
Engine claimed lighter than old one and bigger in cubic inches; current turbo may be too small for 427

power_adder.note: caption turbo sizes ('46', '108') garbled, not usable

failure_modes: head gasket lift at ~30 psi with 18 deg timing on junkyard LS with stock-style studs
